newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says Japan may beef up banking law over DKB.
newsitem.headline: MOF says Japan may beef up banking law over DKB.

text.p: Japan may consider strengthening punitive measures under its banking law after the facts concerning Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd's links to racketeers become clear, Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told a news conference on Monday.

Asked whether the ministry had plans to revise its inspection method and to strengthen punishment under the banking law after the DKB incident, Ogawa said the facts must first be made clear before such changes could be considered.
"We will consider what improvements can be made in our inspection method on clarifying the facts concerning this unusual incident," Ogawa said.
The banking law was drawn up with the purpose of checking for efficient management and healthy financial conditions, and not with the aim of finding criminal acts, he said.
Punishments under the law were also set so that effective inspections could be carried out for such a purpose.
"It is certainly possible to consider whether the current legal framework is sufficent for an effective inspection as we go about clarifying the facts," he said.
Last week, DKB was raided by prosecutors investigating the bank's links with a "sokaiya" racketeer who has been accused of taking illegal payoffs from Japan's top brokerage, Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
